issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter missing @MainActor annotation
issues.description: The rule requires that classes interacting with UIKit or performing UI updates must be marked with @MainActor annotation. The SettingsTextFormatter class formats text for UI display in settings screens but lacks the @MainActor annotation.
issues.rule_name: UI-Related Code Must Be Annotated with @MainActor

issues.title: Incorrect localized string reference in SettingsTextFormatter
issues.description: The formatStudiesText method references strings.detailTextStudies instead of strings.detailTextStudiesV2. This causes the formatter to display the old v1 Studies message ('%@ may install and run studies from time to time.') instead of the new v148 message ('%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone.') that was added in this PR. The helper class was clearly intended to format the new v148 strings based on the PR context, but uses the wrong string constant.

issues.title: Inconsistent format specifier documentation in RolloutsSettingMessage comment
issues.description: The comment for RolloutsSettingMessage incorrectly documents the format specifier as '%1$@' (positional format) while the actual value string uses '%@' (simple format). This mismatch creates confusion for localization teams and could lead to incorrect translations, as translators may attempt to use positional formatting based on the comment when the string implementation doesn't support it. The comment should match the actual format specifier used in the value field.

public static let RolloutsSettingMessage = MZLocalizedString(

        tableName: "Settings",
        value: "%@ will improve features, performance, and stability between updates. Changes applied remotely.",
        comment: "A short description that explains that Mozilla may change features remotely. %1$@ is the app name (e.g. Firefox).")

issues.title: Linter exclusion points to wrong message key version
issues.description: The linter configuration exclusion was updated to reference 'Settings.Studies.Message.v148' but the original PR added this key to exclude quotes validation for the v136 message. Since the PR adds new v148 strings with similar content containing quotes, the exclusion should have remained as v136 to maintain the existing exclusion, or both versions should be excluded. This change will cause the linter to fail validation on the v136 string that legitimately needs the exclusion, while potentially missing issues in the new v148 string.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter class missing final keyword
issues.description: The newly added SettingsTextFormatter class violates repository Rule #12 from AGENTS.md, which requires classes that are not designed for subclassing to be marked with the 'final' keyword. This helper class is clearly not intended for inheritance (it has a private initializer and is a simple utility class), but lacks the final modifier. This prevents compiler optimizations and fails to communicate design intent explicitly, violating an explicit compliance rule added in this same PR.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter and its methods lack explicit access control
issues.description: Rule requires explicit access control modifiers. The new nested class and its members use default (implicit) access levels (`class`, `static let shared`, and `func` declarations have no explicit `internal`/`private`/`public`).
issues.rule_name: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter should be marked final
issues.description: The helper singleton class is not designed for inheritance but is declared as a non-final class. Per the rule, such classes must be marked `final` to prevent unintended subclassing and enable compiler optimizations.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31198 - EXP-5874 Add strings for Rollouts toggle and update Studies strings

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds v148 localized strings for the split "Studies" / "Rollouts" settings toggles in Firefox iOS (Strings.swift plus en-CA/en-GB Settings.strings) and the equivalent keys in Focus's UIConstants. It also adds a linter quotes exclusion for the new Studies message. The Firefox iOS part is a straightforward string-only addition that follows the repo's versioned-key convention.

The Focus part has some problems. It adds dead code (an unused `SettingsTextFormatter` class whose `formatStudiesText` references the old, soon-to-be-replaced string rather than the new V2 one), an unused `detailTextSendUsageDataV2`, and rewrites the comments on existing, already-localized keys (curly to straight quotes), which will churn translator-facing metadata. The Rollouts comment in Strings.swift uses `%1$@` while the other comments use `%@`.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The Firefox iOS string additions are fine. The Focus changes include unused, inconsistent helper code and unrelated comment rewrites on existing keys, which don't belong in a strings-only PR and should be cleaned up.

architecture.overview:
Firefox iOS localizes strings through `MZLocalizedString` definitions in `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift`, with versioned keys (e.g. `.v136`) exported to `Settings.strings` files. Focus iOS defines its strings separately as `NSLocalizedString` calls in `UIConstants.strings`. This PR adds the v148 keys for the split of the Studies toggle into Studies and Rollouts, as a base for follow-up UI work in PR #30988.

No UI consumes the new strings yet. The Firefox side only adds definitions plus en-CA/en-GB catalog entries, and the l10n linter is told to skip the quotes check for the new Studies message. The Focus side adds string definitions and a new helper class that is not wired in anywhere.
steps: Existing entry: `Strings.swift` holds `StudiesSettingTitleV2/LinkV2/MessageV2` (v136 keys) that the Studies settings UI uses today.
New Firefox strings: `StudiesSettingTitleV3/LinkV3/MessageV3` and `RolloutsSettingTitle/Link/Message` with `.v148` keys are added in `Strings.swift`.
Catalog files: en-CA and en-GB `Settings.strings` get the same six keys.
Linter: `linter_config_ios.json` excludes `Settings.Studies.Message.v148` from the quotes check.
Focus: `UIConstants.strings` gains V2/Rollouts strings, existing comments have their quote characters changed, and a `SettingsTextFormatter` helper is added but not used.

findings.title: SettingsTextFormatter is dead code and uses the old Studies string
findings.body:
The new `SettingsTextFormatter` singleton has no callers anywhere in the repo. It also doesn't fit a strings-only PR. `formatStudiesText` formats `strings.detailTextStudies` (the old "may install and run studies" text) rather than the new `detailTextStudiesV2`. Whoever eventually uses it would get the outdated copy.

A singleton class wrapping a `String(format:)` call also adds little over calling `String(format:)` at the call site. The existing Focus code does that directly.

::diff{file="focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift" lines="417-431"}

Remove the class, or if it's needed, make it use the V2 string and add it in the PR that uses it.
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift` (around lines 417-431), remove the unused `SettingsTextFormatter` class. It has no callers, and `formatStudiesText` formats the old `strings.detailTextStudies` instead of `detailTextStudiesV2`. If it is kept, make it use `detailTextStudiesV2` and add it in the PR that actually uses it.

findings.title: Existing Focus string comments rewritten (curly → straight quotes)
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift` lines ~202 and ~205, restore the original curly-quote comments on `detailTextSendUsageData` and `detailTextStudies` (“Firefox Focus” / ”Firefox Klar”) so existing localized keys are not modified. Use the same quote style in the new V2 and Rollouts keys, matching neighbouring entries.

findings.title: Unused detailTextSendUsageDataV2 duplicates the existing string
findings.body:
`detailTextSendUsageDataV2` (`Settings.detailTextSendUsageData.v2`) has identical text and comment to `detailTextSendUsageData`, and nothing in the PR or the description relates it to Studies/Rollouts. A new key with the same English value forces re-translation and leaves an orphan key. Drop it unless a follow-up genuinely needs it.

::diff{file="focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift" lines="203-203"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift` line 203, remove `detailTextSendUsageDataV2`. It is unused and its value and comment are identical to `detailTextSendUsageData`, and it is unrelated to the Studies/Rollouts split.

findings.title: Rollouts message comment uses %1$@ while the value uses %@
findings.body:
The comment for `RolloutsSettingMessage` says `%1$@`, but the value and the other comments, including the matching en-CA/en-GB catalog comments, use `%@`. The comment in `Strings.swift` is therefore out of sync with the `.strings` files. The `.strings` comments are generated from the Swift comment, so they will diverge on the next export.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift" lines="6256-6260"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift` for `RolloutsSettingMessage` (around line 6260), change the comment's `%1$@` to `%@` so it matches the value and the comments in the en-CA/en-GB `Settings.strings` files.

findings.title: Rollouts strings not alphabetically ordered in Settings.strings
findings.body:
The en-CA/en-GB `Settings.strings` files are alphabetically sorted by key, as exported. The new `Settings.Rollouts.*` entries are placed after `Settings.Studies.*`, where `Rollouts` should sort before `Siri`/`Studies`. The next export will reorder them and create diff noise. This is minor, but check how the file is generated.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Shared/Supporting Files/en-GB.lproj/Settings.strings" lines="238-261"}
findings.fixPrompt: In the en-CA and en-GB `Settings.strings` files, move the new `Settings.Rollouts.*.v148` entries so the file stays sorted alphabetically by key, matching the export order. Don't change the content.

findings.title: Firefox iOS strings follow the versioned-key convention
findings.body: The new Firefox keys use the `.v148` suffix, so the existing v136 keys remain stable for translations. Comments include the `%@` placeholder explanation. The linter exclusion is scoped to the single key rather than being a global relaxation. This is a good base for the follow-up UI PR.
